analysis:
Documentation-only change to docs/reference/configuration.md. The visible base units (lines 939-1436) cover the cluster runtime facts table, the coordinator-paired member section, model approvals, link setup/fix and the GPU-limit section. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the full changed set is not visible. Changed ranges are base/head 969, 977-978, 1115 and 1712-1713; only the line 969 hunk is shown in the excerpt.

The visible change expands the `resource_policy_sha256` description. When the build declares a resident tensor assistant public for the model (Qwen3.8-27B: depth 3, `admitted_target_cohort_v1`), the digest additionally covers `qwen27_tensor_assistant_v1`, depth, the `--tp-mtp-inventory-sha256` value, the verification value and the evidence report SHA-256. This binds the assistant configuration into the build-pinned approval digest, which is consistent with the existing pinning model (T-054, A-017). It does not change a trust boundary, introduce code, or loosen any check.

The unseen hunks at 977-978, 1115 and 1712-1713 could not be verified. Line 1115 in base is the 'Changing' row, which mentions that `ClusterConfiguration.validate` refuses a saved `tensorAssistant` beside `nativeMember` ("Qwen's speculative assistant serves local clusters only"). If the head text relaxes that restriction, it would be a real behavior change affecting pair serving. That cannot be confirmed from the supplied evidence. The base text at 977-978 only describes `evidence_sha256` and `qualified_at`. Cross-file questions for integration: whether the code (ClusterPublicModels.tensorAssistant, ClusterPublicTensorAssistant, ClusterConfiguration.validate) matches the doc, and whether the tensorAssistant refusal under nativeMember still holds. The coordinator's matching derivation of the digest is platform-owned and out of scope. No concrete security regression is identified from the visible evidence.
